summary: Iteration 2: verified both HIGH-priority fixes from iteration 1 are working (brute-force lockout returns 429 on 6th wrong login; JTI blocklist causes /auth/me to return 401 after logout with same access token). Ran full backend pytest suite (14/14 passing) and full mobile-first frontend E2E (landing -> register -> 6-step quiz -> result -> save -> dashboard -> settings -> export -> delete). All flows work. One minor UX deviation from spec found on account deletion redirect.

ui_bugs.issue: After clicking settings-delete-confirm-btn, user lands on /login instead of / (Landing). Cause: Settings calls setUser(false) then nav('/'), but ProtectedRoute (still mounted on /settings) re-renders first with user===false and issues <Navigate to='/login' replace/>, overriding the nav('/'). Account IS deleted correctly and cookies are cleared; only the final URL differs from the spec.

action_items: OPTIONAL: To land on '/' after delete as specified, in /app/frontend/src/pages/Settings.jsx call `nav('/', { replace: true })` BEFORE `setUser(false)` (or use window.location.assign('/') to bypass Router race). Alternatively make ProtectedRoute skip the redirect when the target route is already navigating away.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: `set_auth_cookies` uses secure=True and samesite=none unconditionally; fine for the Emergent HTTPS preview but will break plain-HTTP local dev. Consider deriving from an env flag.

server.py: `/routine/generate` calls `upsert_profile(body, user)` as a normal coroutine but the route uses a Depends() signature — works because it's called explicitly here, but the direct call is fragile; extracting the DB upsert into a plain helper would be cleaner.

auth.py: brute-force `check_lockout` only fires when count >= max AND locked_until in the future. After lockout window ends, count is not reset until a successful login; a subsequent single failure will immediately re-lock (count 6 -> 7, locked_until re-armed). Acceptable but slightly aggressive; consider resetting count when window expires.

AuthContext.logout(): does not clear any local state beyond user (fine here, but ensure any cached routines / profiles in sessionStorage are cleared on logout — sessionStorage `le_rituel_last_routine` currently persists across users).

rca of the issue: Post-delete redirect race: /app/frontend/src/pages/Settings.jsx executes `await api.delete('/account'); setUser(false); toast; nav('/');` inside deleteAccount. Because Settings is wrapped by ProtectedRoute which reads `user` from context, the moment setUser(false) commits, ProtectedRoute renders <Navigate to='/login' replace/> BEFORE the nav('/') push is picked up by react-router. The Navigate wins, so the browser lands on /login. Reproduction: register a user, go to /settings, click delete-init then delete-confirm, observe final URL is /login. Mitigation: call `nav('/', { replace: true })` before `setUser(false)`, or use `window.location.replace('/')` to force a full navigation before the ProtectedRoute redirect. Impact: cosmetic — the account is genuinely deleted, cookies cleared, and both /login and / (Landing) are valid unauthenticated destinations.
